s1.syndrome_frame: A subcutaneous mass with recent growth and tenderness on the lower leg
salient_findings: Painful nodule on the lower part of the right leg
Enlargement and tenderness of the lesion over the past 6 months
Irregular, firm, erythematous, mobile, tender mass
key_facts: 40-year-old man
Lesion initially stable in size and painless for 4 years
No history of trauma
No personal or family history of malignancy
Mass measuring 3.5 × 2.3 × 1.7 cm
No popliteal or inguinal lymphadenopathy
Normal routine blood tests
Negative tests for hepatitis B surface antigen and HIV
Lobulated, tan-gray, firm mass on gross examination
Dermal tumor extending into the superficial subcutis
Nests and fascicles of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells on light microscopy
Mitotic figures, including atypical forms, measured 7–8 per 10 high-power fields

shortlist.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
shortlist.why_kept: The tumor's location in the dermis and subcutis, its composition of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells, and its strong positivity for vimentin are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Epithelioid sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: The tumor's epithelioid cell morphology and its expression of melanocytic markers such as Melan-A and HMB-45 are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Pleomorphic hyalinizing angiectatic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: The tumor's location in the subcutis, its composition of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells, and its collagenous stroma are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: The tumor's high mitotic rate and its lack of specific differentiation markers are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Atypical fibroxanthoma
shortlist.why_kept: The tumor's location in the dermis, its composition of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells, and its high mitotic rate are consistent with this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The tumor's initial stability in size and painlessness for 4 years, followed by enlargement and tenderness, along with its location on the lower leg and histological features of nests and fascicles of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells, are consistent with Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans, a rare skin cancer known for its slow growth and local recurrence.

rejected.label: Epithelioid sarcoma
rejected.why: While it shares some histological features, Epithelioid sarcoma tends to occur in younger patients and often has a more aggressive course.

rejected.label: Pleomorphic hyalinizing angiectatic tumor
rejected.why: This tumor typically has a distinct hyalinizing vascular pattern, which is not mentioned in the case description.

rejected.label: Undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma
rejected.why: The presence of specific histological patterns and immunohistochemical staining results in this case do not support a diagnosis of Undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma, which is more heterogeneous and lacks distinct differentiation.

rejected.label: Atypical fibroxanthoma
rejected.why: Atypical fibroxanthoma usually occurs in sun-damaged skin of older adults and has a more superficial location, which does not match the description provided.
